name: Maldives
headline: Maldives: +6.3% growth in 2025, 3.5% inflation, debt 129% of GDP
sections: Maldives is a $7.8 billion economy (2025), the world's 164th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.3% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $29K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 1.8% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 3.5% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges. Unemployment stood at 4.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 129% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 150% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.6% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −6.1% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 156% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 11.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 131% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 81.3 years (2024). Population: 411 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
